description: Hi! We are Computer Science and Information Technology student from Philippines. We specialized in everything.
summary:
VERDE (Visual Environmental Research & Data Explorer) is a web platform for exploring ocean climate trends in the Verde Island Passage and coastal areas of Batangas, Philippines. We developed an interactive, location-based website that uses NASA ocean observations from NASA Earthdata, NASA Worldview, and the NASA Ocean Biology DAAC to visualize how ocean conditions, such as sea surface temperature, change over time, with the source and date of the data shown.

For the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, VERDE selects Earth science variables, focuses on specific coastal regions, and presents time-series views so users can see where and how conditions are changing.

This matters because warming seas and coral bleaching threaten the livelihoods of fisherfolk and coastal communities, yet satellite data is scattered and hard for non-experts to interpret. VERDE turns it into clear, accessible visuals that support awareness, education, and conservation. It complements, and does not replace, official advisories and scientific monitoring.
details:
What it does: VERDE (Visual Environmental Research & Data Explorer) is a web platform that turns NASA ocean observations into clear, location-based insights for the Verde Island Passage and coastal areas of Batangas, Philippines. Users explore an interactive coastal map, select a location, and view time-series visualizations of ocean conditions such as sea surface temperature, with the data source and date shown. This helps users see where and how conditions are changing. It uses NASA data accessed through NASA Earthdata, NASA Worldview, and the NASA Ocean Biology DAAC. It also includes a community reporting workflow and short conservation guidance.

Benefits and intended impact: Satellite data on warming seas and coral bleaching risk is scattered across many platforms and hard for non-experts to read. VERDE puts it in one accessible place so fisherfolk, students, local governments, and conservation groups can understand conditions near them and take informed action. In the long run, we want the platform to expand to other Philippine coastal areas.

Tools: We built VERDE as a web application using JavaScript, interactive web mapping with GeoJSON, and charting tools for time-series visualization, deployed publicly on Vercel.

Creativity: VERDE connects scientific data with local communities. Instead of a technical data portal, it gives people a place-based view of their own coast, paired with community observations and practical conservation actions. Our tagline is “Explore the Blue. Preserve the Green.”

Factors we considered: We showed the source and date of all information so users can trace it. VERDE complements, and does not replace, official advisories and scientific monitoring, and it does not diagnose coral bleaching or pollution on its own. We kept the scope achievable for a two-day hackathon by focusing on one region and a core set of features, and we designed the interface for non-experts.
